trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR (reported, not fixed — MAJOR, mathematical). THE BRAID WORD GIVEN FOR THE FIGURE-EIGHT CLOSES TO THE UNKNOT. The proof writes 'the figure-eight knot 4_1 = sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0^{-1} sigma_1, verified by comparing eigenvalue structure'. That word is the commutator [sigma_0, sigma_1^{-1}]. Settled exactly with content/pipeline/braid-alexander.ts on 3 strands: Alexander(sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0^{-1} sigma_1) = 1, i.e. 'matches: unknot'; whereas Alexander(sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1}) = t^2 - 3t + 1, i.e. 'matches: 4_1'. The closure has one component either way, so a component-count check passes it — only the Alexander polynomial separates them. Correct word (0-indexed, as this block indexes): sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1} = (sigma_0 sigma_1^{-1})^2; 1-indexed: (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^2. This is a SECOND LIVE SITE of a defect already adjudicated on the sibling block figure-eight-branching-rule.md (see its .qa.json, which additionally shows the tabulated chi_{[2,1]} there matches the commutator, not 4_1) and which is the case named in braid-alexander.ts's own module docstring; the sibling was flagged, this block was not. Everything downstream in this proof that reads 'A = 3 nuclei are figure-eight' inherits it, including the closing identification of Vol(4_1) = 2.030 with the binding scale. VERIFIED CORRECT in the same block: Vol(4_1) = 2*Cl_2(pi/3) = 2.02988321 -> '2.030'; and hbar_q^2 = Vol(4_1)/(m_mu/m_e) is the CAL-2 identity — 2.02988321/206.7682827 = 0.0098171885, against hbar_mu^2 = (1 - 1/1.10997859555733471)^2 = 0.0098171885 (exact to 9 digits at the muon pin; 2.1e-7 relative off the proton pin, i.e. the mu-p tension, so the identity is stated on the ideal CAL-2 layer, correctly).
